The Climate Plan puts Brazil on the path of becoming a sustainable, resilient, safe, fair and prosperous country, with governments, civil society, the private sector and the conscious scientific community, engaged and acting in an integrated way in the face of climate change.

The overall objective of the Climate Plan is to guide, promote, implement and monitor coordinated actions aimed at the transition to an economy with zero net emissions of greenhouse gases by 2050 and the adaptation of human and natural systems to climate change, through short, medium and long-term strategies, in the light of sustainable development and climate justice.
increasing resilience of populations, cities, territories and infrastructure in the face of climate emergency
promote sustainable and resilient production and regular access of the population to healthy foods in adequate quality and quantity
promoting water security, providing water in sufficient quality and quantity for multiple uses, such as supply, production, energy and ecosystems
protect, conserve, restore and strengthen ecosystems and biodiversity, and ensure the provision of ecosystem services
promoting, protecting and recovering the health and well-being of populations, respecting the ways of life of traditional peoples and communities
ensuring energy security in a sustainable and accessible way
promoting socioeconomic development and reducing inequalities
protect cultural heritage and preserve cultural and local heritage practices, facing the risks related to climate change
strengthen the vital role of the ocean and the coastal zone in coping with climate change.
